title: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting - Cultural and Creative Arts - Materials, Tools, Equipment
exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In the process of producing a craft work, consumable items that are ultimately transformed into the finished product are known as:
questions.explain: Materials are the raw, consumable supplies (like wood, clay, thread) that are physically transformed or used up to create a finished craft work.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following correctly defines a 'tool' in craft production?
options: A heavy, immovable machine used in a factory.
A hand-held implement used to carry out specific operations on a material.
The consumable items that make up the finished artwork.
The final decorative product displayed on a wall.
questions.explain: Tools are handheld implements like chisels, scissors, and spatulas used by a craftsperson to shape or work on raw materials.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Identify the primary raw material required for the Tie and Dye process.
questions.explain: 100% cotton fabric is highly recommended for tie and dye because natural fibers absorb and retain dye solutions far better than synthetic ones.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Clay, plastercine, and paper pulp are specific materials mainly utilized in which craft?
questions.explain: These are all pliable, plastic materials used specifically for moulding objects like pots, figures, and vases.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of these materials is abundantly used for weaving local baskets in Nigeria?
questions.explain: Palm fronds and raffia are flexible plant materials traditionally stripped and dried for weaving baskets and mats.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Apart from wood, what other affordable household material is commonly used by JSS students to practice carving?
questions.explain: Key soap (a firm bar soap) is frequently used in Nigerian classrooms to introduce students to the subtractive techniques of carving because it is soft and easy to cut.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Cardboard and paper gum are classified as essential materials for producing:
questions.explain: Paper gum (an adhesive) and cardboard (stiff paper) are standard raw materials used in executing paper crafts like models, kites, or greeting cards.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following implements is a sharp hand tool primarily used by carvers to shape wood?
questions.explain: A chisel is a tool with a characteristically shaped cutting edge, used along with a mallet to carve or cut hard materials like wood and stone.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In a craft workshop, heavy machinery or fixed setups that facilitate production, such as a potter's wheel, are best described as:
questions.explain: Equipment refers to the heavy, durable, and often stationary machineries (like kilns or potter's wheels) that assist in production but are not held in hand or consumed.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Dye stuff is an essential consumable item required in which of the following crafts?
questions.explain: Dye stuff (coloring agent) is heavily used in fabric crafts such as tie and dye and batik to give vibrant colors to plain cloths.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following items is NOT considered a raw material in craft production?
questions.explain: A hammer is a tool used to apply force. Unlike clay, dye, or soap, it does not become a permanent part of the finished craft, nor is it consumed.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Identify the piece of equipment commonly used in weaving traditional textiles (e.g., Aso-oke).
questions.explain: A loom is a piece of equipment used to weave cloth and tapestry by holding warp threads under tension to facilitate the interweaving of weft threads.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
